title: Nine Pots — the rival kiln hamlet west of Sill
caption: The pottery hamlet eight leagues west of Sill, drawn at walking scale along the road of the old feud: four kilns and one shared clay pit, the potters' houses and worked strips, the moot-post, and the road east forded over the Ferr toward Sill. Stonemouth stands three leagues east where the Ferr meets the Ilm, with its lime kilns and coarse sandstone workings; the blue-grey Lead Run comes in from the west, and the Rim Road passes north on its way to Keld Keep. Sill and Greybank are drawn faint at the east edge for neighbourhood only. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Ember, with compass, a league scale in paces, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the feud, the lime and sandstone trade, the Lead Run that makes a man thin, and a cord from the Fishstairs never carried upriver. An engraved pot counted out at Nine Pots sits in the margin.
